title: Independent helpline and oversight for abuse and harassment reports in public healthcare
asked: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong asked whether MOH will consider establishing an independent and centralised helpline or oversight under the Tripartite Framework for the Prevention of Abuse and Harassment in Healthcare, to enhance follow-up and accountability of internal reporting of abuse in all public healthcare institutions for all non-police cases.
response: Dr Koh Poh Koon said all public healthcare institutions have internal mechanisms for due follow-up of reported abuse or harassment, including immediate incident response, post-incident management and support for affected staff, and follow-up actions against perpetrators. A Tripartite Workgroup with MOH, unions and healthcare employers meets regularly to share best practices. He said MOH and the Government have a zero-tolerance stance, hospitals report perpetrators to the Police, and internal handling is kept because hospitals are best placed to assess incidents involving patient confidentiality and mental capacity. Staff who feel a hospital has not been fair can escalate to MOH for a separate independent review.

key_points.point: All public healthcare institutions have internal mechanisms to ensure due follow-up of reported abuse or harassment.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: all public healthcare institutions have put in place internal mechanisms to ensure due follow-up of reported cases of abuse or harassment.

key_points.point: Internal mechanisms include immediate incident response and reporting, post-incident management with support for affected staff, and follow-up actions against perpetrators.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: These include protocols for immediate incident response and reporting, post-incident management including support provided to the affected staff, and follow-up actions against perpetrators.

key_points.point: The Tripartite Workgroup for the Prevention of Abuse and Harassment of Healthcare Workers includes MOH, unions and healthcare employers from public, community care and private sectors, and meets regularly to share best practices.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: The Tripartite Workgroup for the Prevention of Abuse and Harassment of Healthcare Workers, comprising the Ministry of Health (MOH), union and healthcare employers from public healthcare, community care and private healthcare sectors, also convenes regularly to share best practices on the management of abuse and harassment cases.

key_points.point: MOH and the Government take a zero-tolerance stance against abuse of any healthcare workers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: MOH and the Government takes a zero-tolerance stance against abuse of any healthcare workers.

key_points.point: Hospitals report perpetrators to the Police for further investigation and take actions against them.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: hospitals do even report perpetrators to the Police for further investigation and take actions against them.

key_points.point: The process is kept internal because hospitals are in the best position to make a judgement.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: there are real reasons why we keep this process internal to the hospital, because they are in the best position to make a judgement.

key_points.point: If staff believe a hospital has not been fair, they can escalate to MOH, which will take a separate independent review.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: If there is a concern that the hospital has not been fair to the staff, they can escalate it to MOH, where we will take a separate independent review on this as well.

left_open: Whether an independent and centralised helpline or oversight under the Tripartite Framework will be established for all non-police cases.
How follow-up and accountability of internal reporting would be enhanced across all public healthcare institutions.
supplementary: Concerns about independent and centralised handling of abuse and harassment reports, including possible hospital conflict of interest.
